summary:
Deep dive on `yg check` output (release/6.1.0 dist in the dev container). I produced these states in $TMPDIR/chkout-* scratch projects: a fresh init, a 24-node synthetic graph (deterministic refusals, advisory refusals, pending LLM pairs, a broken relation, a missing description, unmapped files, the log gate, broken node YAML, broken yg-config.yaml, an invalid architecture file, a status downgrade, a progressive/reference-branch run), a full clone of the Yggdrasil repo at scale (473 nodes, 4383 unverified pairs), and a real canon-sync refusal in a private repository that carried the family's canon check at the time (read-only, installed 6.0.0). I ran every mode: plain, --top/--top N, --summary, --details, --aspect, --json, --approve --only-deterministic, --approve --dry-run, a pseudo-TTY run and FORCE_COLOR. I also read check-render-header/groups/views.ts, group-issues.ts, check.ts, fill-log-gate.ts, fill-progress.ts, fill-dry-run.ts and the message sources.

Overall verdict: the what/why/next data model is sound, but four things make the output hard to read.
1. The renderer has at least five different grammars. Grouped, details, unmapped, gate-abort and flag-error output each label (or don't label) Why/Fix/Next differently.
2. Volume is unbounded for agents, because non-TTY output is never truncated and even --top and --summary don't bound it.
3. The information hierarchy is inverted. Mechanical, fillable 'unverified' groups come first. Graph-invalidating errors (config/architecture/YAML) are buried mid-report, and the rest of that report is quietly computed on a degraded graph.
4. Engine-side messages carry renderer-specific whitespace and splice hacks. That produces misaligned lines, run-on sentences and dangling colons.

JSON is not a structured alternative: violations and unmapped file lists exist only as prose inside `what`/`report`. Also, the writer path's gate abort emits zero bytes on stdout under --json.

surviving.title: Non-TTY output (what agents see) is never truncated; the sanctioned narrowing views --top and --summary don't bound it either
surviving.where: source/cli/src/cli/check-render-groups.ts:466 (`const truncate = opts.isTTY && blockMembers.length > CAP_NODES`); check-render-views.ts renderTopBody/renderSummaryRows; templates/rules.ts:96
surviving.evidence: On a clone of the Yggdrasil repo ($TMPDIR/chkout-self, fresh clone, det cache empty): `yg check` > 4398 lines / 338,416 bytes, one group `unverified (not yet reviewed)  4377 pairs  435 nodes` followed by 4377 bullets. `yg check --top` (bare = 'just the single suggested-next group') prints the SAME 4377-bullet group, because the one group is the whole wall. `yg check --summary` = 448 lines / 38,910 bytes. `yg check --json` = 4,794,050 bytes (issues 2.29 MB, the same 230-char `why` repeated in 4377 issue objects). `yg check --approve --dry-run` = 9219 lines. Under a pseudo-TTY the same group truncates to 12 bullets plus `... and 12 more` (chkout-b). Humans get the cap and agents get everything. Meanwhile the agent rules (rules.ts:96) say: 'never pipe it through | grep, | head, or | tail … When the output is still large, the SANCTIONED way to narrow it further is yg check --summary … or yg check --top [N]'.
surviving.impact: The agent following the protocol has no way to get a bounded answer. It reads ~85k tokens for a state whose whole meaning is '4383 free deterministic pairs need filling', or it breaks the no-head rule. --top only bounds the number of groups, not the size of a group, so on a real repo --top N and plain check are the same size. The TTY-only cap also means humans and agents see structurally different reports.
surviving.suggested_fix: Cap the members per group in every mode, TTY or not: show N bullets, then `… and K more (yg check --aspect <id> | --details)`. Make --top N bound the members too, and collapse same-shape members (see CO-4) into `aspect X on 24 nodes: svc-01…svc-24`. For unverified groups, summarise by aspect × kind (`self-contained-references: 612 file pairs (deterministic, free)`) rather than listing pairs. Summary rows should drop zero fields. Put the full enumeration behind --details/--json only.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. check-render-groups.ts:466 is `const truncate = opts.isTTY && blockMembers.length > CAP_NODES`, so the cap applies only on a TTY, and the doc comment at :356 says so ('[TTY-only…]'). This is deliberate, but it defeats the narrowing path that rules.ts:96 sanctions. On a fresh local clone of chkout-self ($TMPDIR/verify-check-output-self), `yg check --top` gave 4389 lines / 337,801 bytes: the one group `unverified (not yet reviewed)  4377 pairs  435 nodes` with every bullet listed, then `(no warning groups within --top 1 …)`. `--json` came to 4,794,063 bytes and `--summary` to 448 lines / 38,910 bytes. On the 24-node fixture, `--top` (non-TTY) printed all 24 log-entry-missing bullets. Under `script -qc` the same group ended at `... and 12 more`. So humans get a capped view and agents get the full list. --summary also prints all-zero fields (`(repo)  0 unverified (0 deterministic-free, 0 LLM), 0 refused, 2 other`).

surviving.title: The --approve gate abort (log gate) uses a different, unlabelled, ungrouped grammar, prints no report, and emits an empty stdout under --json
surviving.evidence: In $TMPDIR/chkout-b (24 log_required nodes, no entries), `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` printed to stderr 24 repetitions of three bare lines, e.g. `No fresh log entry for node 'app/svc-01' — mandatory before recording verdicts when its source drifted.` / `Node type 'service' has log_required: true — every source change needs a justification entry capturing WHY. This component's source has drifted from the state its recorded verdicts were written over, which earlier commits can be as much the cause of as anything in progress now. Recording answers for the code as it stands, so it stops here and approves nothing this run until a fresh entry exists.` / `yg log add --node app/svc-01 --reason '<justification>', then re-run: yg check --approve`. The identical ~400-char why appears 24 times. There is no header, no count, no Why:/Fix: labels and no verdict line; stdout had 0 lines. The same run with `--json` gave stdout 0 bytes and stderr 14,533 bytes. These nodes had never had a verdict, yet the text claims their source 'drifted from the state its recorded verdicts were written over'. The re-run hint drops the `--only-deterministic` the user typed.
surviving.impact: The most common first --approve failure on a log_required graph is the least readable output the CLI produces, and it looks nothing like `yg check`. A JSON consumer (Horde reads `yg-check/1`) gets no document at all and has to scrape stderr prose. An agent following the hint escalates from the keyless lane to the paid lane.
surviving.suggested_fix: Route gate aborts through the same grouped renderer: a `yg check --approve: ABORTED  (24 nodes need a log entry)` header, one group with the shared why printed once, a templated fix (`yg log add --node <node> --reason '…'` for: svc-01 … svc-24), and a Next line that preserves the user's flags. Under --json, always write a yg-check/1 document with exit.status `aborted` and the gating issues. Word the why conditionally (never verified vs drifted).
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-check-output-b2 after removing the LLM aspect, so the in-flight keyless/config-reviewer-missing abort is not what fires. `yg check --approve --only-deterministic`: stdout 0 bytes, stderr 73 lines / 14,418 bytes. That is a `Filling 50 unverified pairs…` line followed by 24 bare three-line blocks with no labels, header or count, and the ~400-char why is repeated identically each time. The why says 'This component's source has drifted from the state its recorded verdicts were written over' although these nodes never had a verdict. The hint is `yg log add --node app/svc-NN … then re-run: yg check --approve`, which drops --only-deterministic. With `--json`: stdout 0 bytes, stderr 14,418 bytes. In source, fill-log-gate.ts:45-50 hardcodes that text, check.ts:527 sends emitIssue to stderr, and the FillGatingError branch (check.ts:569-573) only calls exitAfterFlush(1) and writes no document. Plain `yg check` words the same condition differently ('its source changed but no justification entry exists'). This is distinct from the in-flight suggestedNext item, which covers infra failures and merge conflicts.

surviving.title: Graph-invalidating errors are buried mid-report, and the rest of that report is computed on a degraded graph with no warning; Next still points at --approve
surviving.where: source/cli/src/cli/group-issues.ts:176-206 (ERROR_CODE_PRIORITY ranks log-entry-missing, unverified and aspect-violation-enforced above every STRUCTURAL code); check-render-views.ts formatOutput (no degraded-graph banner)
surviving.evidence: (a) Appending `quality: [` to yg-config.yaml (chkout-c): the `config-invalid` block first appears at line 73 of the report, after the 24-bullet unverified group and both enforced groups. The header silently changes shape from `26/32 files (26 node-owned, 0 type-covered, 0 excluded)` to `26/32 files (81%)` because the config fell back to defaults. The last line is `Next: yg check --approve  (fills 24 unverified; 13 errors remain — need code/graph fixes)`. (b) Adding an invalid type to yg-architecture.yaml: `Errors (37) in 5 groups` drops to `Errors (4) in 2 groups`. The unverified group vanishes because the architecture's aspects are no longer attached, so the report looks greener when the architecture breaks, and `architecture-invalid` sits between `enforced` and `unmapped`. Its text also says `Why: yg-architecture.yaml failed to parse` / `Fix: Fix the YAML syntax` for a schema error (`must have a non-empty 'description' string`). (c) A broken svc-10/yg-node.yaml: the header reads `24 nodes` (the node silently disappears), `yaml-invalid` is the 4th group, and Next is `yg check --approve (fills 23 unverified; 14 errors remain …)`.
surviving.impact: The one error that invalidates every other line is the one a reader is least likely to reach. An agent follows Next, fills verdicts against a fallback config or a missing architecture, and records work it will have to redo. It reads 'fewer errors' as progress.
surviving.suggested_fix: Add a top tier: config-invalid, architecture-invalid, yaml-invalid and lock-invalid render first, directly under the header. Add a banner saying the report ran on a degraded graph ('yg-config.yaml did not parse — defaults used; 1 node not loaded; results below are partial'). Make suggestedNext name the fix for that error. Rank structural and graph errors above fillable unverified pairs in the group order too. Use different text for a parse error and a schema error.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced all three variants on copies of a clean fixture (baseline: `Errors (101) in 6 groups`). (a) Appending `quality: [` to yg-config.yaml: `config-invalid` appears at line 86, after log-entry-missing and the unverified group. The header changes to `26/33 files (79%)` and unmapped grows from 2 to 7 because coverage.required was lost. The report gives no degraded-config banner. (b) An arch type missing its description: `Errors (4) in 2 groups` (down from 101), architecture-invalid sits between unverified and unmapped, and the text is `Why: yg-architecture.yaml failed to parse` / `Fix: Fix the YAML syntax` for a schema error. Next is `yg check --approve  (fills 2 unverified; 2 errors remain …)`. (c) A broken svc-10 yg-node.yaml gives a `24 nodes` header, with yaml-invalid as the 5th group. Also, on my first fixture run an invalid parent `app/yg-node.yaml` produced `0 nodes · 0/32 files`: every child was silently dropped. That makes the degradation worse than the researcher reported.

surviving.title: Per-file pairs inside a node render as identical, indistinguishable bullets because the unit is dropped
surviving.where: source/cli/src/cli/check-render-groups.ts:481 (`renderMemberBlock(group.members, (m) => m.nodePath ?? '')`) plus the memberAspectSeg logic around :440
surviving.evidence: Yggdrasil clone, plain `yg check`: `- cli/ast/report  aspect 'self-contained-references'` printed 6 times in a row, and `- graph-rules  aspect 'self-contained-references'` 14 times. The JSON for the same issues differs only by unit: `"unit": "file:source/cli/src/ast/file-path.ts"`, `"file:source/cli/src/ast/find-comments.ts"`, … The dry-run preview for the same pairs does name them: `[det] self-contained-references on file:source/cli/src/ast/file-path.ts — free`.
surviving.impact: Duplicate lines read as a rendering bug and carry no information an agent can act on. It can't tell which file is unverified or refused without --json. The pair is also named in two vocabularies across modes: `node  aspect 'x'` in the report versus `x on node:y` / `on file:z` in fill progress and dry-run.
surviving.suggested_fix: When a member's unitKey is `file:`, render it: `- cli/ast/report  aspect 'self-contained-references'  source/cli/src/ast/file-path.ts`. Better, collapse per aspect: `self-contained-references ×6 files`. Adopt one pair notation (`<aspect> @ <unit>`) everywhere: report, progress, dry-run, JSON.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced on the self clone. `- cli/ast/report  aspect 'self-contained-references'` appears 6 times, and `- graph-rules  aspect 'self-contained-references'` appears 36 times (the researcher said 14; the real count is higher). The --json issues for cli/ast/report differ only in unit (file:source/cli/src/ast/file-path.ts, find-comments.ts, index.ts, report.ts, types.ts, walk.ts). The cause is check-render-groups.ts:481, `renderMemberBlock(group.members, (m) => m.nodePath ?? '')` when fileCount===0, which drops the file: unitKey. The dry-run names the same pair as `[det] … on node:…`, so the report and dry-run use different notations.

surviving.title: aspect-status-downgrade blames the node and names the downgrading site as the cascade source; one type-level fault is reported 24 times
surviving.where: source/cli/src/core/checks/aspect-contracts.ts:771-777 (`origin: source.origin === own:… ? … : source.origin`), formatters/aspect-status-messages.ts:54
surviving.evidence: The architecture had `service.aspects: [- id: header-comment, status: advisory]`, and no node attached header-comment. The output was 24 bullets, one per service node: `- app/svc-01  Node 'app/svc-01' attaches aspect 'header-comment' with status 'advisory', but the aspect cascades onto this node with status 'enforced' from type:service.` The node attaches nothing. type:service is the site that declared 'advisory'. The 'enforced' anchor is the aspect's own default. The code passes the offending source's own origin as the 'cascades … from' clause.
surviving.impact: This gives the wrong model. An agent edits node files that contain no such attachment, or edits type:service believing it is the enforcing source. The single real fix (the aspect default versus the type attach) never gets named, and 24 copies turn one design error into a wall.
surviving.suggested_fix: Name the actual declaring site and the actual anchor source ('type:service declares advisory; aspect header-comment defaults to enforced; set status: advisory in the aspect's yg-aspect.yaml or remove it from the type'). Report the finding once, at the declaring site, when the declaration is on a type, ancestor or flow, not once per inheriting node.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced exactly. The only attach is `service.aspects: - id: header-comment, status: advisory` on the type, and no node attaches it. Output is 24 bullets of `Node 'app/svc-01' attaches aspect 'header-comment' with status 'advisory', but the aspect cascades onto this node with status 'enforced' from type:service.` In source, aspect-contracts.ts:776 passes `origin: source.origin`, the downgrading source's own origin, into the 'cascades … from' clause. The anchor there is the aspect default (`aspectDef?.status ?? 'enforced'`, :753), and the message template (aspect-status-messages.ts:54) always says 'Node X attaches'. So the text names the wrong actor and the wrong anchor, and one type-level fault is repeated once per inheriting node.

surviving.title: --json has no structure for the data agents act on: violations and unmapped file lists exist only as prose, and why/next are repeated per issue
surviving.where: source/cli/src/formatters/check-json.ts (issues[] carry what/why/next strings; pairs[].report is a newline-joined string)
surviving.evidence:
chkout-b `yg check --json`: `"pairs"[…].report: "src/svc-03/index.ts:1: TODO marker left in shipped code — move it to the tracker
src/svc-03/index.ts:2: …"`, even though check.mjs returned `{file,line,column,message}` objects. The unmapped issue reads `"what": "2 source files not covered by any node.
  src/orphan/a.ts
  src/orphan/b.ts"` with no files array (the text renderer has issue.uncoveredFiles). relation-broken's `why` contains `
     Existing nodes under app: svc-01, …` with baked-in whitespace. On the Yggdrasil clone the identical unverified `why` is repeated in 4377 objects (4.8 MB document).
surviving.impact: Machine consumers (Horde, CI annotators, agents choosing --json to save tokens) must regex-parse English to get file:line or the uncovered file list. JSON costs more tokens than the text view it is meant to replace.
surviving.suggested_fix: Within yg-check/1 (adding fields is free per family-contracts), add `violations: [{file,line,column,message,expected?,actual?}]` on refused pairs and issues, `files: []` on coverage issues, and `data` fields for structured hints (e.g. `suggestions`). Emit why/next once per code or group (e.g. a `groups[]` array with shared why/next and member refs) instead of per issue.
surviving.verifier:
Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-check-output-d.json. pairs[].report is one newline-joined string (`"src/svc-01/README.md:3: [canon-sync] …
    expected: …"`). `unmapped-files` has what=`"2 source files not covered by any node.
  src/orphan/a.ts
  src/orphan/b.ts"` and no files array. relation-broken's why contains `
     Existing nodes under app: svc-01, …`. It is worse than reported: `uncovered-advisory` what in JSON truncates at 5 files (`"… ap.err
... and 2 more"`), so the machine document loses data that the text view lists in full. On the self clone there is 1 distinct `why` across 4383 issues (4.79 MB).

surviving.title: Refusal blocks explain the cache, not the rule, and use a drifting label vocabulary (enforced / refused / advisory); Fix and Next duplicate each other
surviving.where: formatters/lock-issue-messages.ts:74-75; cli/group-issues.ts:239-240 (labels 'enforced'/'advisory'); check-render-views.ts:488
surviving.evidence: Every deterministic refusal group reads `enforced  8 pairs  8 nodes  aspect 'no-todo'` / `A deterministic check recorded these violations. The result is cached — the same inputs reproduce the same verdict, so the check is not re-run.` / `Fix: Fix the listed violations, then: yg check --approve` / `- app/svc-03  Violations:` followed by the list. The aspect's own description ('unfinished work belongs in the tracker, not in shipped code') never appears. The same finding is called `enforced` (grouped label), `refused` (--summary, progress `— refused`), `is refused on node:app/svc-01 by a deterministic check` (--details) and `aspect-violation-enforced` (JSON code). `Violations:` dangles after the node name. The warnings-only PASS ends with `Next: Fix the listed violations, then: yg check --approve`, a verbatim copy of the Fix line above it.
surviving.impact: The 'why' slot, the most valuable place to teach the agent the rule's intent, is spent on engine trivia. A reader sees the label 'enforced' and has to infer that it means 'violated'. The same fact under four names makes cross-view reading and grepping unreliable.
surviving.suggested_fix: Use the aspect description (first sentence) as Why for refusals. Keep 'cached' only in --details or knowledge. Label the group `refused (enforced)` / `refused (advisory)`, the same word in every view and as a JSON `verdict`. Put the violation list directly under the node without the `Violations:` token. Fix text: `Fix the violations below, then re-run`. Next should add information beyond Fix (e.g. the concrete first file:line).
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. Refusal groups read `enforced  8 pairs  8 nodes  aspect 'no-todo'` / `A deterministic check recorded these violations. The result is cached — the same inputs reproduce the same verdict, so the check is not re-run.` / `Fix: Fix the listed violations, then: yg check --approve` / `- app/svc-03  Violations:`. The aspect description never appears. The fill progress line says `— refused`, and the JSON code is `aspect-violation-enforced`. The final line `Next: Fix the listed violations, then: yg check --approve` repeats the Fix line word for word (it is also the JSON suggestedNext).

surviving.title: expected:/actual: payloads render as two unwrapped single lines of 500–1500 chars with no diff marker
surviving.where: check-render-groups.ts renderMemberBullet (continuation lines passed through verbatim); the check.mjs violation contract has only a free-text `message`
surviving.evidence: A private repository's `yg check --no-approve` (the family canon check, 6.0.0): `expected: "**Three jobs, one core, in layers.** … registered on [one page](…)"` and `actual:   "…"`, each about 1500 chars, ×4 repos. Reproduced on 6.1.0 in chkout-b (`canon-sync`): two ~560-char lines where the only difference is `Adoption runs Grain first, then` versus `Adoption runs Grain first — install it day zero — then`, around character 480. The line also repeats the location: `src/svc-01/README.md:3: [canon-sync] src/svc-01/README.md:3 differs from canon`, because the renderer prefixes file:line and authors put it in the message too.
surviving.impact: A human can't find the difference without copying both strings into a diff tool. An agent pays for about 2×N×1500 chars to learn about a six-word change. This is the concrete source of the 'checks are hard to read' observation.
surviving.suggested_fix: Accept optional structured `expected`/`actual` on a violation. The renderer then prints a compact word-level diff with context elision (`… Adoption runs Grain first[-,-]{+ — install it day zero —+} then …`). JSON keeps both full strings. Document that the engine adds file:line, so messages should not repeat it.
surviving.verifier: The rendering is real: two ~560-char unwrapped `expected:`/`actual:` lines differing only by `— install it day zero —`. But the layout, and the repeated `[canon-sync] path:line` prefix, are written by the check authors, not by Yggdrasil. The fixture's check.mjs builds that message, and the family's canon sync check (family-sync-check.mjs:200, now `ws check canon-sync`) builds `${repo.name}/README.md:${fileLine} differs from canon\n    expected: …\n    actual: …`. The renderer only passes the free-text message through. What remains on Yggdrasil's side is a missing feature: the violation contract has no structured expected/actual field and no diff rendering. That is not a defect in yg's own output.

surviving.title: Engine messages carry renderer-dependent whitespace and splice hacks, which produce misaligned lines, run-on sentences, dangling colons and dropped lines
surviving.where:
core/checks/relations.ts:51,53 (`
     Existing nodes…`, `
     Did you mean`); core/check-coverage-phase.ts:62-66 (splices a sentence onto next line 0 'because the renderer shows only next.split(
)[0]'); core/check-coverage-tiers.ts:126; check-render-groups.ts first-line-only member rendering
surviving.evidence: relation-broken renders `            This node declares a dependency that cannot be resolved.` then `     Existing nodes under app: svc-01, … svc-24`, indented 5 columns inside a 12-column block, and suggests `Did you mean 'app'?` (a module) for target `app/svc-99`. Unmapped Fix: `Fix: Check ownership candidates: yg context --file <path> yg type-suggest --file <path> can help design one before you decide where it belongs.` Two commands run together with no separator. The following line `Then: add to existing node mapping, or create a new node.` exists in JSON `next` but is never shown in text. type-without-when-with-mapping members end in a dangling colon: `- app/svc-01  Node 'app/svc-01' has type 'service' (no `when` — organizational type) but mapping is not empty:` with the file list cut off. yaml-invalid's code frame prints `  mapping: [` and `^` at column 0 under an indented block. The renderer owns indentation, wrapping and lists. Render multi-line `what` for all codes, or never emit multi-line `what`. Add a lint or test that no messageData string contains leading spaces after a newline.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. relation-broken prints `     Existing nodes under app: svc-01, …` at column 5 inside a 12-column block and suggests `Did you mean 'app'?` for target `app/svc-99`. Unmapped prints `Fix: Check ownership candidates: yg context --file <path> yg type-suggest --file <path> can help…` as one run-on line. The JSON next carries a second line, `\nThen: add to existing node mapping, or create a new node.`, that the text view never shows. type-without-when members end with a dangling `but mapping is not empty:`. `Your architecture has no type for this file yet.` appears next to multi-file lists. surviving.title: No single visual grammar: labels, headers, counts and plurals differ across blocks, views and paths
surviving.where: check-render-groups.ts:394 (grouped shared why has no 'Why:' label) vs :204/:247/:340 (labelled); :387 (`${pairCount} pairs  ${countSeg}`); check-render-views.ts:319 (aspect header); check.ts:324; fill-dry-run.ts:89
surviving.evidence: Grouped blocks print the why unlabelled (`Orphaned aspects add noise …`). Single, unmapped and repo-level blocks print `Why: …`. The next step appears as `Fix:`, `Next:`, `Next (this group):`, `Run:` (flag errors), `Nothing to fix —` (progressive notice), or an unlabelled third line (gate abort, `Notice:`). Headers: `yg check: FAIL  25 nodes · …` vs `FAIL  (aspect 'no-todo' — 8 of 37 errors)`. Plurals: `yg-node.yaml … 1 pairs  1 nodes`, `Filling 2 unverified pairs across 1 nodes`, `(fills 2 unverified; 1 error remain …)`, `Pruned 2 stale verdict(s) — 0 billed, 2 free`, `0 reviewer call(s) is an UPPER BOUND`. 'pairs' is counted for non-pair findings (`description-missing  1 pairs  1 nodes`, `log-entry-missing  24 pairs`). Stacked parentheses: `unverified (not yet reviewed) (outside changes)`, `unmapped (outside changes) (2)`. The header count unit differs from the body: `PASS (3 warnings)` over a body listing 2 advisory violations plus 4 uncovered files. TTY truncation of a code-only group says `... and 12 more` with no drill command. `--top 0` gives `Error: --top expects a non-negative whole number; got "0".`
surviving.impact: A reader can't learn one pattern and scan. An agent can't key on stable tokens: 'Why:' is sometimes absent, and the next step has six spellings. Grammar slips reinforce the impression of unreadable output.
surviving.suggested_fix: Define one block grammar in a single module and use it for check, fill-abort, notices and flag errors: `<LABEL> <count> <subject>` / `  why: …` / `  fix: …` / members. Always label, use one next-step keyword, and share one pluralize helper. Count issues in one unit (findings) and show the file count inside the block. Merge parenthetical qualifiers (`unverified · outside changes · 2 files`).
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. `description-missing  1 pairs  1 nodes` and `log-entry-missing  24 pairs  24 nodes`. Grouped whys are unlabelled, while config-reviewer-missing, unmapped and uncovered use `Why:`. summary:
Surface sweep of the live 6.1.0 CLI (dev-container dist, `yg --version` still prints 6.0.0). I ran every top-level `--help` (28 commands) and captured a help page, a representative run and a typical error for check (plain, --approve --only-deterministic, --approve --dry-run, --json, --summary, --top, --top N, --details, --aspect), prime, advise, log add/read/merge-resolve, tree, owner, node, context, impact, aspects, --health, flows, find, type-suggest, suppressions, simulate, structure, incident, knowledge, schemas, drill, aspect-test, portal, pack, marketplace, adopt and init --upgrade. I used three projects: an empty dir, a small scratch project seeded with real defects ($TMPDIR/uxsweep-a) and a fresh clone of the Yggdrasil repo itself ($TMPDIR/uxsweep-ygg, 473 nodes). I checked renderer source where it explained what I saw.

Overall: there is no shared visual grammar. `yg check` has at least five header forms and three block layouts. The what/why/next content exists almost everywhere, but it is rendered differently everywhere: labelled, unlabelled, missing the Why: label, or as a NEXT heading. Seven variants of the next-step label appear. Errors have no single prefix, casing or stream contract.

The worst readability problems:
- Agents (non-TTY) get uncapped member lists. On a real repo, `--top` prints 4,392 lines.
- A rule violation, the most important finding, is headed by the rule's status word `enforced`.
- The same advice is repeated three or four times on every run, including green runs.
- `--summary` collapses every non-verdict error into the count `other`.

The JSON surface covers 7 of about 28 commands. It carries prose instead of fields, is sometimes less complete than the text, and errors are never JSON. Exit codes are only 0 and 1 by rule. The in-flight items listed in the brief are not repeated below.

summary:
Agent-consumption audit of the yg CLI on release/6.1.0, using the dev-container dist on scratch copies of the Yggdrasil repo (473 nodes) and of the examples no-secrets-in-logs, layered-architecture and checkout-flow. Some outputs are cheap and clean: a green `yg check` is one line of 119 bytes, and a realistic 2-file edit prints 48 lines (3.6 KB). The problems start when an agent reads the output through a pipe or asks for machine output.

- **Caps apply only on a terminal.** The size caps work only when output goes to a terminal, so an agent (piped, not a TTY) gets the whole list. `--top` does not shorten a group's member list either, and prime forbids piping to head/tail. On a fresh clone that is 338 KB, where a terminal shows 2 KB.
- **`--json` is huge and cannot be narrowed.** It always includes every approved pair and refuses `--top`/`--summary`: 4.8 MB on a fresh clone, 2.46 MB for a 33-issue edit.
- **Text and JSON do not carry the same facts.** Text drops the file for file-scoped pairs, which leaves duplicate bullet lines. It also drops the second line of the unmapped fix. JSON, for its part, keeps violations, relation edges and file lists only inside prose strings.
- **`Next:` can point at the wrong thing.** It can name a symptom instead of the root cause (a YAML error in one node shows up as a 'non-existent node' with 'create the missing node'). `suggestedNext` is sometimes a runnable command, sometimes prose with placeholders, sometimes several lines.
- **Labels do not match codes.** A refusal is labelled 'enforced'. `--summary` puts relation, log and coverage errors under 'other', then says 'Fix the listed violations' in a view that lists none.
- **Advise and relation messages confuse who must approve.** They say 'your approval' / 'their approval' / 'requires confirming', and an agent may read itself as the approver.
- **Error and next-step wording differs from command to command** (Error:/Run:/Fix:/Next:/Then:/none).
- **`yg tree` is 290 KB with no compact or JSON form,** yet prime and several errors send agents to it.
- **Knowledge topics cannot be read by section.** `cli-reference` is 94 KB, prime sends agents there for every flag and never mentions `--help`, and wrapping differs between files and splits inline command spans across lines.

Findings already in flight (the unverified/stale label, prime length, `yg verdict` references, `--approve` after infra failures) are not repeated.

surviving.title: Caps are TTY-only, so agents (piped) get unbounded check output, and the 'sanctioned' narrowing flags do not narrow

surviving.evidence: Fresh copy of the Yggdrasil repo (deterministic cache gitignored, so 4377 unverified pairs), `yg check --no-approve` piped to a file: 4398 lines, 338,416 bytes (~85k tokens). For code-only groups such as `unverified`, fold members per node (`cli/ast/report  13 pairs (12 det, 1 LLM)`) instead of one line per pair.

surviving.title: --json always carries every pair (approved ones included) and refuses every narrowing flag: megabytes for a handful of issues

summary:
Design baseline and code structure of the output layer (Yggdrasil release/6.1.0, dist run in the dev container). The main finding is that there is no output layer. The CLI never uses console.*. It prints through 258 process.stdout.write and 145 process.stderr.write calls spread over 33 and 29 files. chalk is imported in 29 files and styles are picked ad hoc (93 chalk.red, 37 green, 26 dim, 24 yellow, 7 bold). The only shared formatter for what/why/next is formatters/message-builder.ts, 12 lines that return `${what}\n${why}\n${next}`. The line `process.stderr.write(chalk.red(`Error: ${buildIssueMessage(...)})` is copied at 96 sites in 21 files, and 7 files each define their own failWith/emitError copy. The check report has its own 1,500 lines of rendering (check-render-header/groups/views.ts). advise, marketplace, log, fill progress (written from core/, the engine) and tree each use their own layout. The repo's what-why-next aspect governs the content of the triad but explicitly allows labelled or unlabelled rendering and exempts report output, so no rule governs how output looks. That gap is why the owner finds the output hard to read: 5+ layouts for the same triad, 3 names for one field (next / Fix: / Next:), prose used as control flow, TTY-only truncation that gives agents the full wall, and hand-rolled plurals and caps.

What a single output module needs:
(1) A Diagnostic type: severity, stable code, subject (node or node›file), a one-line summary kept apart from detail lines, why, and fix as { command?: argv, text }. It replaces the free-text IssueMessage at render time.
(2) One renderer per target: human text (colour, emoji and caps allowed), plain agent text (no colour, same caps plus an explicit drill command, stable porcelain grammar) and JSON (with the same error envelope on failure).
(3) Shared primitives: section(title, count), list(items, {cap, drill}), count(n, noun), kv, note, progress. Engine code emits events, never strings.
(4) A code registry: code → label, gloss, knowledge topic, noun for counts.
(5) Tests that assert on the intermediate document tree plus a few golden files, not on indentation heuristics.

Reference CLIs, and what fits here. rustc/cargo: the `error[code]: summary` / `--> subject` / `= note:` / `= help:` grammar with stable codes and `--explain`. It maps directly onto code + what + why + fix, with `yg knowledge` as the explain target, and cargo's closing line ("N errors; M fixable with …") is the model for a cost-annotated Next:. terraform plan: one fixed-category summary line ("Plan: 2 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy") is the model for the check header and a real --summary. eslint stylish: findings grouped by subject, one line per problem, rule id at the end, and a final "✖ N problems (E errors, W warnings) / K fixable with --fix". That fits member bullets, which should name the unit and never repeat. gh: TTY and non-TTY are both deliberate. Piped output is terser and structured (and --json takes a field selection), never "the TTY text without caps"; Yggdrasil has this inverted. git status: short inline hints ("use git add … to update") and a separate, stable --porcelain format. That argues for a versioned plain grammar agents can rely on, separate from human wording. Also: an explicit --color=auto|always|never, and an emoji/colour gate separate from truncation.

Evidence: live dist runs in scratch projects (a fresh shallow clone of the repo and a small keyless project with one refusing deterministic aspect, one undeclared relation and one organizational-type mapping), plus file:line reads. The in-flight items the orchestrator listed are not repeated here.
